answer: A remote attestation registry curbs Sybil identities by binding agents to certified hardware enclaves. At the dawn of each epoch, nodes submit signed attestation quotes verified against a decentralized identity atlas. An adversary seeking to fabricate agents incurs the non-fungible capital cost of purchasing physical secure silicon per identity. However, manufacturer centralization and microarchitectural side channels can harbor undisclosed vulnerabilities that weaken validation guarantees.
